name: Naturpark Zillertaler Alpen
kurzbeschreibung: The High Mountain Nature Park Zillertal Alps features over 80 glaciers, pristine side valleys, the mountaineering village of Ginzling, and immense biodiversity.
preis: Nature park area and themed trails freely accessible; exhibitions at Nature Park House partly chargeable
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; Nature Park House in Ginzling open daily from mid-May to late October
beschreibung:
Overview

The High Mountain Nature Park Zillertal Alps spans 422 square kilometers across pristine high-alpine wilderness, extending from the mountaineering village of Ginzling up to the glaciated summits of the Zillertal main ridge at 3,509 meters. As an internationally recognized protected area, the nature park encompasses more than eighty glaciers, rugged cirques, crystal-clear mountain streams, and deeply carved side valleys including the Zemmgrund, Zillergrund, and Stilluptal. Thanks to massive elevation differences and diverse geology, the park provides habitats for over nine thousand documented animal and plant species, including golden eagles, ibexes, marmots, and rare alpine flora. The modern Nature Park House in Ginzling serves as the central hub and visitor center, showcasing an impressive exhibition on the geological formation, mineral treasures, and cultural alpine history of the region.

Route & Requirements

The protected area offers over five hundred kilometers of well-marked hiking and high-alpine trails for all fitness levels. Leisure hikers enjoy gentle walks through shady larch and pine forests along the themed nature trails around Ginzling. Seasoned mountain hikers frequently tackle sections of the challenging Berlin High Trail (Berliner Höhenweg) or ascend to historic mountain refuges such as the Berliner Hütte, a protected monument of early alpine club history (walking time approx. 3 hours from Breitlahner, moderate T2). For all high-altitude mountain routes, sturdy ankle-high hiking boots with reliable vibram tread, wind- and waterproof jackets, and sufficient alpine awareness are required. Guided theme hikes with certified nature park rangers are offered throughout the summer months.

Visit & Arrival

The nature park is accessible year-round, while mountain huts and higher trails operate between mid-June and early October. By public transport, take the Zillertalbahn train from Jenbach to Mayrhofen, followed by frequent regional buses (lines 4102 and 4104) directly to Ginzling and popular valley trailheads. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 to the Zillertal exit and continue along the B169 through Mayrhofen to Ginzling. Paid hiker parking lots are available at Breitlahner and Schlegeis reservoir.

Tips

Combine a valley walk with a visit to the mineral exhibition at the Nature Park House in Ginzling to marvel at rare smoky quartz and garnet crystals discovered in local crevices. Afterward, indulge in homemade Kaspressknödel soup on the terrace of an authentic mountain refuge.
